raw_response:
I am old now, and there are only two of us at home, so I cannot spread myself too thin. Cotton needs many hands for picking, and wheat-maize is the steady way here, so this year I will keep most land in wheat-maize for safety and leave a smaller piece in cotton for cash. I will do 12 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 12 mu, and 8 mu in cotton. I do not read rates from papers. I farm by what I have seen on my own land and what the neighbors do. Wheat cannot be too hungry, or yield falls badly, so I will not cut fertilizer too much there. Maize I plant quickly after wheat harvest, no delay, because missing the season is worse than doing rough land prep. Cotton can make money, but it takes labor, so I will keep it on fewer mu and not push too hard with inputs. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate wheat first, then give maize and cotton water only when the weather really asks for it.
